title: Launch to Adoption: 90-Day Experiments Playbook
content:
Purpose: capture a pragmatic, experiment-first 90-day onboarding plan that our CSMs can run as a lightweight sprint. Goal is to surface high-impact operational levers (integration steps, example prompts, routing config) and measurable adoption experiments so we can shorten time-to-value and create clear renewal signals.

Audience: CSMs, Solutions Engineering, Onboarding Ops, Customer Success Managers handling mid-market and enterprise accounts.

High-level approach: treat the first 90 days as three 30-day sprints, but emphasize short experiments (1–2 weeks) that can be validated quickly. For each sprint include: hypothesis, owner, activation steps, metrics, success criteria, and fallback.

Key outcomes we want by day 90:
- Core integration completed and validated (API keys, model selection, routing policy configured).
- Product-level usage at 3x baseline for targeted workflow (e.g., support triage, content generation).
- Two documented prompt templates and one evaluation set feeding Redwood Optimize.
- Clear renewal intent signal defined (usage thresholds, feature enablement, exec sponsor engagement).

Roles and responsibilities:
- CSM (owner): coordinates onboarding sprints, runs weekly sync, owns customer comms and QBR prep.
- Solutions Engineer: configures initial model/routes, sample prompts, assist integration tests.
- Customer Engineer / SE: helps with code snippets, SDK onboarding, infra checks (VPC, keys).
- Onboarding Ops: tracks experiment cadence, logs results in registry, escalates blockers.
- Account Executive (if present): engages at milestone 2 to align renewal/account expansion signals.

Sprint 0: Pre-start checklist (before day 0) — complete within 1 week of kickoff
- Confirm stakeholders and exec sponsor (CSM)
- Share onboarding plan and meeting cadence (CSM)
- Collect technical details: environment, region, expected QPS, data classification (SE)
- Create first ticket in experiment registry: "Launch -> Baseline usage" (Onboarding Ops)
- Quick smoke test: issue a sample generate request using the customer key (SE)

Sprint 1 (Days 0–30): Integration + Baseline Measurement
Hypothesis 1: If we deliver a working sample integration and two example prompts tailored to the customer workflow within 2 weeks, devs will run baseline tests and produce measurable API calls within 10 days.
Owner: Solutions Engineer / CSM
Critical tasks:
- Day 0: Kickoff w/ stakeholders; agree success metrics for 30/60/90 (CSM)
- Day 2–5: Provide SDK snippet + repo example for preferred stack (SE)
- Day 6–12: Deliver 2 customer-specific prompt templates + test harness (SE)
- Day 13–18: Live integration support session; validate end-to-end (CSM + SE)
- Day 20–30: Capture baseline: unique users, API calls/day, token counts, average latency (Onboarding Ops)
Metrics to track:
- Time to first successful API call (target < 48 hours)
- Baseline daily active users (DAU) and sessions for target workflow
- Tokens per success flow and average latency
Success criteria for Sprint 1:
- Working end-to-end demo in customer environment
- Baseline metrics captured and entered into experiment registry
Fallbacks: if integration stalls >7 days, escalate to engineering-on-call and shift to a 'proxy integration' using a simple webhook shim.

Sprint 2 (Days 31–60): Feature adoption experiments and routing/cost tuning
Hypothesis 2: Small config changes (batching, cache TTL, model variant) will improve cost-per-inference by >=20% without harming core UX.
Owner: CSM + Onboarding Ops + SE
Experiments to run (1–2 week cycles):
- Experiment A: Enable prefix KV cache for repeated prompts; measure latency and token reduction
- Experiment B: Try lower-cost quantized model variant for background tasks; measure quality via eval set
- Experiment C: Progressive batching policy for non-latency-critical calls (nightly bulk runs)
Measurement plan:
- Create evaluation prompt set (10–20 cases) and register in Redwood Optimize
- Track cost per meaningful response (tokens * unit $) and NPS-style internal feedback from devs
Success criteria for Sprint 2:
- At least one cost optimization proving >=15% unit-cost reduction with acceptable quality tradeoff
- Two adoption nudges implemented (example: scheduled digest emails, in-app reminders)
Renewal signal triggers to observe in Sprint 2:
- Sustained DAU > baseline +20% for 7 consecutive days
- Exec sponsor replies to value check with plan to expand usage or budget

Sprint 3 (Days 61–90): Scaling, QBR prep, and renewal positioning
Hypothesis 3: If we show operational readiness (SLOs, rollback plan, A/B safety fallback) and a clear ROI summary, the customer will commit to a renewal or expansion conversation.
Owner: CSM + AE + Onboarding Ops
Tasks:
- Week 9: Operational readiness checklist (SLOs defined, error budgets, fallback model)
- Week 10: Draft QBR one-pager: usage growth, cost delta, quality signal, next-step recommendations
- Week 11: Run a lightweight internal risk review (SRE + Product) to validate resilience for targeted scale
- Week 12: QBR with customer and renewal next-step (CSM + AE)
QBR talking points template (short bullets):
- Headline: "X% growth in usage since baseline; Y tokens/day; average token cost Z$"
- Wins: two operational improvements (caching, model variant) and measured impact
- Risks: any latency spikes, integration fragility, data retention issues
- Ask: decision on renewal window and intended scale (target DAU, budget)

Renewal signals (strong, moderate, weak)
- Strong: active exec sponsor + usage growth >50% and documented plan to expand feature set.
- Moderate: steady usage > baseline +20% and positive SE feedback; no exec confirmation.
- Weak: intermittent usage, still in POC, open technical debt items.

Experiment registry (quick format to use in Confluence/Jira)
- Title | Hypothesis | Owner | Start | End | Metric(s) | Result | Notes
- Example row: "KV cache for customer X | caching reduces tokens by 30% | Marco D. | 2025-11-15 | 2025-11-29 | tokens/response, latency | success (26% reduction) | saw no QA regressions on eval set"

Communication templates (short snippets to copy)
- Kickoff email subject: "[Customer] Redwood onboarding kickoff: goals and 90-day plan"
- Integration follow-up: "Thanks — attached SDK snippet and two prompt templates. Can we validate a sample call by EOD Friday?"
- QBR invite: "Quarterly Business Review: discuss usage, ROI, and next steps. 30 min"

Open questions / decisions to make (CSM TODO list)
- Who will own the long-term model selection policy? (Product or Customer?)
- If a customer wants on-prem/private deploy in sprint 2, what is the minimum lead time? (work with Private Deployments team)
- Decide renewal cadence for accounts that finish onboarding mid-cycle (align with AE).

Risk ladder and escalation flow
- Low: single integration error — CSM/SE triage within 24h
- Medium: recurring errors > 3% of calls or latency above SLO — escalate to SRE and Onboarding Ops; weekly sync
- High: data loss, security incident, or major throughput outage — immediate incident bridge with SRE and Product; pause rollout and notify customer execs

Measurement artifacts to populate (spreadsheet columns)
- date, active_users, api_calls, avg_tokens_per_call, avg_latency_ms, cost_per_day_usd, feature_flag_state, exec_contacted (Y/N)

Quick checklist to attach to customer record (CSM copy)
- [ ] Exec sponsor identified
- [ ] SDK snippet shared and validated
- [ ] Two prompt templates committed to repo
- [ ] Eval set uploaded to Redwood Optimize
- [ ] One cost optimization test completed
- [ ] QBR one-pager drafted
- [ ] Renewal signal assessment completed

Appendix: micro-experiment ideas (for inspiration)
- Incentivize devs with a lightweight "first-10-calls" badge + Slack bot notification to the team
- Run a short A/B of two prompt phrasings to measure mean user satisfaction for generated output (collect simple thumbs up/down)
- If customer has a content catalog, try embeddings to speed similarity search and measure query latency improvements

Notes to self: keep this doc lean. Move concrete experiment results into the central registry (linked above). After two customers complete this flow, convert the successful experiments into a short playbook checklist per industry (SaaS-support, marketing automation, search).

Last updated by Sophie Nguyen on 2025-12-08.
